evolution_chain.description: Original 1872 Civil Code enactment; single paragraph; common-law codification
Added subdivision (b) employer vicarious liability rule
Added subdivision (c) statutory definitions with 'despicable' threshold; deleted 'express or implied' from (a); added subdivision (e)
Added subdivision (d) homicide-based wrongful death. No amendments 1988-2026.

case_law.holding_summary: Conscious disregard of known risks can constitute § 3294 malice without specific intent to injure. Categorical treatment of drunk driving; narrowed post-1988 but core doctrinal holding survives.
Plaintiff must introduce evidence of defendant's financial condition at the punitive phase; without such evidence, any punitive award is reversed on appeal.

case_law.citation: College Hospital Inc. v. Superior Court (1994) 8 Cal.4th 704
case_law.holding_summary: 'Despicable' means vile, base, contemptible, miserable, wretched, or loathsome; ordinary negligence plus foreseeable harm is insufficient post-1988.

Modern synthesis of BMW/State Farm federal due process guideposts; reprehensibility is the most important factor; ratios above 9:1 permitted for extraordinary reprehensibility; potential-harm anchoring.

citizen_relevance.target_case: 2958 Honeysuckle house sale (multi-year dispossession pattern, intentional fraud, vulnerable victim)
citizen_relevance.punitive_track: FRAUD track under § 3294(c)(3) — avoids despicability threshold; OPPRESSION track as alternative based on multi-asset dispossession pattern
citizen_relevance.ratio_analysis: Reprehensibility profile (intentional, multi-year, vulnerable victim, financial motive) supports ratio above 9:1 under Bankhead/Simon framework; potential-harm anchoring across the full dispossession pattern permits larger absolute award
